questions.question: State the accounting equation, explain why double entry follows from it, and give the compass for the five account types.
questions.expected_answer: Assets equal owner's equity plus liabilities — what the business owns is financed by the owner and by outsiders, at every moment. Because the equation must stay level, every transaction has two equal effects, a debit and a credit: double entry is the equation defending itself. Compass: assets, expenses and drawings increase on the debit side; owner's equity, liabilities and income increase on the credit side. Example: a R15 000 capital deposit debits Bank (asset up) and credits Capital (equity up), leaving the equation level.

questions.question: Post Lerato's month and prove it with the trial balance, naming what the level scale cannot see.
questions.expected_answer: Bank: in 15 000 + 7 500 + 1 200 = 23 700, out 6 500 + 2 000 + 1 200 + 2 500 = 12 200, balance R11 500 dr. Trading stock: 6 500 + 4 000 + 400 in, 6 000 + 2 000 out, R2 900 dr. Debtors control 2 500 − 500 − 1 200 = R800 dr. Creditors control 4 000 − 2 500 = R1 500 cr. Sales 7 500 + 2 500 − 500 = R9 500 cr; cost of sales 6 000 + 2 000 − 400 = R7 600 dr; rent 2 000, wages 1 200, capital 15 000. Trial balance: debits 11 500 + 2 900 + 800 + 7 600 + 2 000 + 1 200 = 26 000 = credits 15 000 + 9 500 + 1 500. Equal totals prove the double entry held but cannot see an amount posted to the wrong account or a transaction omitted on both sides.

questions.question: Explain the control-account check and match each error to the record it disturbs.
questions.expected_answer: The control account is built from journal totals; the individual customer pages from individual postings — the same street counted twice by different routes, forced to agree monthly. Debtors: control 2 500 − 500 − 1 200 = R800, equal to Mr Naidoo's page (2 500 − 500 − 1 200 = R800); creditors: control R1 500 matches the wholesaler's page. Errors: a receipt on the wrong customer's page disturbs the list but not the control; a miscast journal column disturbs the control but not the list; an invoice never posted to the individual account leaves the list short. Each disagreement points at its own kind of error — two independent witnesses telling the same story is what makes the books believable.
